content.text: No exclusivity obligation binds us anywhere in the agreement; the capacity provisions expressly confirm freedom to deal with other carriers, so the preferred position is met and no redline is warranted.

input.quote: any Party is entitled to make available any of its Allocated Capacity for use by other Carriers on any commercial basis without any restrictions.
input.rationale: The agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on us, so it sits at the preferred position. Searches for exclusivity language returned only the "sole and exclusive remedy" wording in the dispute-resolution clause (p0262), which is a remedies/forum term belonging to GOVLAW and not a purchasing restriction. The capacity provisions run the other way: Paragraph 12.20 (p0206) and Paragraph 12.22 (p0208) expressly entitle any Party to sell IRU to, and make its Allocated Capacity available for use by, other Carriers "without any restrictions", and Paragraphs 15-17 require open transiting, interconnection and Direct Access rights for other Carriers. Nothing requires us to source capacity or services solely from the other APCN 2 Parties or to refrain from procuring from third parties. The pre-trigger conditions on private IRU sales (Paragraph 12.21, Annex 7 use/Transfer conditions) restrict onward resale of our own allocated capacity rather than our freedom to buy from other suppliers, and Paragraph 12.1's "can only be used by a carrier" limits the class of permitted users, not our sourcing; neither is an exclusivity or sole-supplier covenant. No redline proposed.

mappings.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
